// Generated from framework/contracts/author/src by `bun run contracts:generate`.
// Do not edit by hand.
// RFC 0005 feature-config-access.md: the process-global feature-config surface.
//
// A `FeatureConfig` (see ./feature-config.ts) is injected into the handler
// contexts that carry one (`chat.config`). This module adds a *process-global*
// counterpart: a bare `config` an author can import directly —
//
//   import { config } from "routekit-eval/config";
//   const raw = await config.read("tui"); // merged local-over-global block
//   await config.write("tui", { theme: "gruvbox" }, "global");
//
// — for the many call sites that have no handler context in scope (module-level
// init, a chat surface's `start()` before any turn). `read(namespace)` returns
// the raw merged file block; `write(namespace, value, scope?)` performs a
// merge-preserving write. Both return the same resolver the injected `config`
// handle resolves in that process.
//
// IMPORTANT — cross-realm rendezvous. The host runtime and a feature's vendored
// `routekit-eval` SDK are SEPARATE module graphs (the feature imports the generated
// `.routekit-eval/sdk` copy, not this source). A plain module-level singleton set by the
// host would therefore be invisible to the feature. So the active resolver lives
// on a well-known `globalThis` slot keyed by a `Symbol.for` registry symbol,
// which every realm shares. The host installs the resolver once per scoped
// runtime (see the CLI config wiring).
//
// Like `routekit-eval/state` and unlike `routekit-eval/logger`, the pre-install default REJECTS
// rather than no-ops: `read`/`write` are file-backed I/O; a silent stub would
// make a feature believe config is absent (falling to defaults) or silently drop
// a persisted preference. So before the host installs a resolver — and in any
// standalone/test context — `read`/`write` reject with a clear error. A feature
// that resolves config at `start()` handles this like any other failed I/O.
//
// This module MUST NOT import `effect` or `@routekit-eval-engine/*`; it ships inside the
// author-facing `routekit-eval` SDK, which is effect-free by contract (RFC 0002 / 0007).
// The host does all Effect bridging on its side before calling installFeatureConfig.

import type { FeatureConfig, FeatureConfigScope } from "./index";

/**
 * The `globalThis` registry key the active config resolver is published under.
 * `Symbol.for` returns the same symbol across every module realm in the process,
 * so the host's install and a feature's `config` calls rendezvous on one slot
 * even though they live in different module graphs.
 */
const FEATURE_CONFIG_GLOBAL_KEY = Symbol.for("routekit-eval/feature-config/v1");

interface FeatureConfigGlobal {
  current?: FeatureConfig | undefined;
}

/** Read (creating on first use) the shared global slot. */
const slot = (): FeatureConfigGlobal => {
  const host: Record<symbol, FeatureConfigGlobal | undefined> = globalThis;
  const existing = host[FEATURE_CONFIG_GLOBAL_KEY];
  if (existing) {
    return existing;
  }
  const created: FeatureConfigGlobal = {};
  host[FEATURE_CONFIG_GLOBAL_KEY] = created;
  return created;
};

const NO_RESOLVER_MESSAGE =
  "no config resolver is available in this context: routekit-eval/config has no resolver installed (call read()/write() from a running feature, not at import time)";

/**
 * The process-global feature-config handle. Always defined; resolves the active
 * resolver on EVERY call (never captures it), so a resolver installed after a
 * module imported `config` still takes effect and `resetFeatureConfig()` cleanly
 * reverts to the reject default. Rejects when no resolver is installed rather
 * than resolving a stub that loses writes or fabricates an absent block.
 */
export const config: FeatureConfig = {
  read: (namespace: string): Promise<unknown> => {
    const resolver = slot().current;
    if (resolver === undefined) {
      return Promise.reject(new Error(NO_RESOLVER_MESSAGE));
    }
    return resolver.read(namespace);
  },
  write: (
    namespace: string,
    value: unknown,
    scope?: FeatureConfigScope
  ): Promise<void> => {
    const resolver = slot().current;
    if (resolver === undefined) {
      return Promise.reject(new Error(NO_RESOLVER_MESSAGE));
    }
    return resolver.write(namespace, value, scope);
  },
};

/**
 * Install the host's {@link FeatureConfig} as the active global implementation
 * and return a restore closure that reverts to the *prior* occupant on release.
 *
 * **Use the returned closure** (not `resetFeatureConfig`) to release the install
 * from a scoped runtime. This saves and restores the previous value, so two
 * concurrent runtimes in one process each release cleanly without blanking the
 * other's install. This is a host-only hook, kept off the bare `routekit-eval` surface so
 * a feature cannot hijack the config slot.
 */
export const installFeatureConfig = (resolver: FeatureConfig): (() => void) => {
  const s = slot();
  const prev = s.current;
  s.current = resolver;
  return () => {
    s.current = prev;
  };
};

/**
 * Unconditionally clear the active global resolver, reverting `config` to the
 * reject default. Use this for hard reset (standalone teardown, test cleanup);
 * prefer the restore closure returned by `installFeatureConfig` for scoped
 * runtimes.
 */
export const resetFeatureConfig = (): void => {
  slot().current = undefined;
};
